newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Arboyne readies for Nonoc project startup.
newsitem.headline: Arboyne readies for Nonoc project startup.

text.p: Arboyne NL said on Thursday that it would change the company's name and increase its authorised capital ahead of the final development of the Nonoc nickel project in the Philippines.

The company, whose shareholders approved a change in name to Pacific Nickel Ltd, said the increase in authorised capital to A$2 billion from A$50 million would allow the company to issue new shares to buy the project.

"These are important changes for the company, as they not only better reflect the principal activities of Pacific Nickel, but also move us considerably closer to taking over and realising the potential of the Nonoc Nickel Project," chief executive officer Steve Kesler said.

Nonoc has been closed since 1986 but was capable of producing 65 million pounds of metal a year. The mine complex was owned by the national government which entered into an agreement in July 1996 for Arboyne to take over the project.

Swiss commodities group Glencore International Ag has agreed to market the nickel and cobalt output while contract conditions were being finalised with Kvaerner ASA for the refurbishment of the refinery, the company said.
It said the next step was to complete the due diligence process dealing with the proposed acquisition of the project and the capital raising to fund the refurbishment and commencement of operations.
